newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: OMV to cut costs at home, expand abroad.
newsitem.headline: OMV to cut costs at home, expand abroad.

text.p: Austria's OMV said on Tuesday it would continue to cut its workforce and domestic gasoline station network this year at the same time as it increased its presence in neighbouring markets.

Director Tassier Peyrer Heimstaett told a news conference OMV aimed to trim its domestic filling station network this year "a little more than last" and reduce the group workforce by five percent after four percent to 8,491 in 1996.
OMV, which posted record earnings in 1996 for the second straight year, first introduced its cost-cutting drive in response to heavy losses in 1992 and 1993.
Last year the number of OMV filling stations in Austria fell to 726 from 800 while the number of stations abroad rose to 332 from 274.
OMV is active in the gasoline retail market in southern Germany, the Czech Republic, Slovakia, Hungary, Slovenia and Croatia.
"By the year 2000 the network should be twice as big as it is today," Peyrer Heimstaett said.
